name: Neptune
headline: diameter
description: Neptune is the eighth and farthest planet from the Sun, an ice giant slightly smaller than Uranus but more massive. Its equatorial diameter is 49,528 km, about four times Earth's. It was found in 1846 from mathematical predictions of where an unseen planet should be.

measures.label: Equatorial diameter
measures.note: Diameter at the equator, at the 1-bar pressure level

measures.label: Polar radius
measures.note: Centre to pole at the 1-bar level (equatorial radius is 24,764 km)

measures.label: Mass
measures.note: Total mass; source states 102.409 x 10^24 kg

facts.text: NASA gives Neptune an equatorial diameter of 49,528 km (30,775 miles), about four times wider than Earth.
If Earth were the size of a nickel, Neptune would be about as big as a baseball.
Neptune was discovered on 23 September 1846 by Johann Gottfried Galle, based on predictions by John Couch Adams and Urbain Le Verrier.
Wind speeds on Neptune reach up to 580 m/s.

caveats: Radii are measured at the 1-bar pressure level, since Neptune has no solid surface.
Neptune is slightly smaller than Uranus in diameter but has more mass (102.409 vs 86.811 x 10^24 kg).
